title: Typed backend services and SQL repositories
summary: One Protobuf contract generates interoperable Go and TypeScript Connect clients/services with shared local HTTP conformance tests, plus an independent generated sqlc Go SQLite repository.

profiles: Linux x86_64, Node 24.19.0 / TypeScript 5.9.3, Buf 1.73.0, Protobuf-ES 2.16.0, Connect 2.2.0: proto lint, descriptor generation/typecheck and 3 real local HTTP protocol tests passed.

Linux x86_64, Go 1.27.2 / Connect Go and protoc-gen-connect-go 1.21.0 / Protobuf and protoc-gen-go 1.36.12: binding generation and 6 Go tests and the race detector passed, including shared conformance, pre-decode auth/body limits, cancellation, error boundaries, redirect refusal and concurrent storage.

Linux x86_64, the pinned Node and Go runtimes above: 2 cross-language HTTP/1.1 Connect tests passed (generated Go client to TypeScript service; TypeScript client to Go service), each using the same 3 create/get, 5 pagination and 10 typed-error cases.
Linux x86_64, Go 1.27.2 / sqlc 1.31.1 / modernc SQLite 1.39.1: query generation and repository transaction, missing-row and cancellation test passed.
notes: Go and TypeScript share a protobuf contract and conformance fixture. Protocol tests cross separate local processes; each service owns its storage. The sqlc Go repository remains an independent persistence profile.

Generated Protobuf and SQL query code, downloaded runtime source and fixture binaries are excluded from delivered files; explicit commands regenerate them using pinned tools. Retain upstream generator/runtime notices and licenses.

The browser client source typechecks; browser/CORS deployment, gRPC, HTTP/2, streaming, production identity/TLS, durable database lifecycle and trusted breaking-change baselines remain receiving-service gates.
